status: Pre-specified 10-seed source/attack-family holdout protocol. CICIDS2017 was used previously in the broader project, but these locked zero-day source-holdout conditions were not used to develop the router.
primary_hypothesis: Classical–Quantum complementarity is attack/distribution dependent; the rate at which Quantum CAT rescues Classical CAT errors can shift materially from known development traffic to zero-day attack traffic.
guardrails: Report all 3 conditions and all 10 seeds.
Do not select only attack families showing increased quantum complementarity.
Do not claim quantum advantage from simulator results.
Do not claim Adaptive HQCA superiority unless supported consistently by effect size and paired tests.
Treat complementarity shift as attack-dependent if direction differs by held-out family.
